translation_en: 'Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated this to me: Bahz narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us with this chain. He added: Then the Prophet put one hand over the other and said: Cut them down completely. The report says they replied: We said that, Messenger of Allah. He said: Then what is my name? No, I am Allah's servant and Messenger.

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me: Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us: Thabit narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Rabah, who said: We came as a delegation to Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and Abu Hurayrah was among us. Each man used to prepare a meal for his companions on one day. It was my turn, so I said: Abu Hurayrah, today is my turn. They came to the house, but our food was not ready. I said: Abu Hurayrah, would you tell us a report from the Messenger of Allah until our food is ready? He said: We were with the Messenger of Allah on the day of the conquest. He placed Khalid ibn al-Walid in command of the right flank, al-Zubayr in command of the left flank, and Abu 'Ubaydah in command of the foot soldiers and the bottom of the valley. He said: Abu Hurayrah, call the Ansar to me. I called them, and they came running. He said: People of the Ansar, do you see the rabble of Quraysh? They said yes. He said: When you meet them tomorrow, cut them down completely. He gestured with one hand over the other and said: Your appointed meeting place is al-Safa. No one came out against them that day without being felled. The Messenger of Allah climbed al-Safa, and the Ansar came and surrounded it. Abu Sufyan came and said: Messenger of Allah, the green force of Quraysh has been destroyed; there will be no Quraysh after today. Abu Sufyan said that the Messenger of Allah replied: Whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe; whoever lays down his weapon is safe; and whoever closes his door is safe. The Ansar said: The man has been overcome by compassion for his clan and longing for his town. Revelation came to the Messenger of Allah. He said: You said that the man has been overcome by compassion for his clan and longing for his town. What, then, is my name? He repeated this three times. I am Muhammad, Allah's servant and Messenger. I emigrated to Allah and to you; my life is with you and my death is with you. They said: By Allah, we said this only from our attachment to Allah and His Messenger. He said: Allah and His Messenger affirm what you say and excuse you.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Amr al-Naqid, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us. The wording is Ibn Abi 'Umar's. They said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Prophet entered Makkah while three hundred and sixty idols stood around the Ka'bah. He began striking them with a stick in his hand, saying: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; falsehood is indeed bound to vanish (17:81). The truth has come, and falsehood neither initiates nor restores (34:49). Ibn Abi 'Umar added: on the day of the conquest.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated this to us, both from 'Abd al-Razzaq: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, with this chain up to the words: bound to vanish. He did not mention the other verse and said idol instead of idols.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir and Waki' narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Mut'i informed me, from his father, who said: I heard the Prophet say on the day Makkah was conquered: After this day, no Qurayshi will be executed in retaliation until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Zakariyya narrated to us with this chain. He added: No one among the rebellious Quraysh had accepted Islam except Mut'i. His name had been al-'Asi, the disobedient, and the Messenger of Allah renamed him Mut'i, the obedient.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to me: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib say: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib wrote the treaty between the Prophet and the polytheists on the day of Hudaybiyah. He wrote: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to. They said: Do not write Messenger of Allah; if we knew you were Allah's Messenger, we would not have fought you. The Prophet said to 'Ali: Erase it. He replied: I am not the one who will erase it. The Prophet erased it with his own hand. Among the conditions they agreed upon was that they would enter Makkah and stay there for three days, and would enter carrying no weapons except weapons in their sheaths. I asked Abu Ishaq what that phrase meant. He said: A sword sheath and what it contains.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib say: When the Messenger of Allah made peace with the people of Hudaybiyah, 'Ali wrote a document between them, writing: Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. He then related something like Mu'adh's hadith, except that it did not mention the words: This is what he agreed to.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and Ahmad ibn Janab al-Missisi both reported from 'Isa ibn Yunus. The wording is Ishaq's. He said: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us: Zakariyya informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara': When the Prophet was prevented from reaching the House, the people of Makkah made peace with him on the condition that he enter Makkah and stay there three days, carrying no weapons except a sword and its sheath; that he take none of its people out with him; and that he not prevent anyone who was with him from staying there. He said to 'Ali: Write the agreement between us: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to. The polytheists said: If we knew you were Allah's Messenger, we would follow you. Instead write Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah. He ordered 'Ali to erase it, but 'Ali said: No, by Allah, I will not erase it. The Messenger of Allah said: Show me where it is. 'Ali showed him, and he erased it and wrote: Ibn 'Abdullah. He stayed there three days. On the third day they said to 'Ali: This is the last day in your companion's agreement; tell him to leave. 'Ali informed him, and he said: Yes, and he departed. Ibn Janab's report says they would have pledged allegiance to you instead of followed you.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: Quraysh made a treaty with the Prophet, with Suhayl ibn 'Amr representing them. The Prophet said to 'Ali: Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Suhayl said: We do not know what In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful means. Write instead what we know: In Your name, O Allah. The Prophet said: Write: From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. They said: If we knew you were Allah's Messenger, we would follow you. Instead write your name and your father's name. The Prophet said: Write: From Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah. They stipulated that if someone from their side came to the Muslims, he would not be returned, but if someone from the Muslims came to them, he would be returned. They said: Messenger of Allah, shall we write that? He said: Yes. Whoever leaves us to join them, may Allah distance him; whoever comes to us from them, Allah will make a way of relief and deliverance for him.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us. Another chain: Ibn Numayr narrated to us—their wordings are close—my father narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Siyah narrated to us: Habib ibn Abi Thabit narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, who said: Sahl ibn Hunayf stood on the day of Siffin and said: People, question your own judgment. We were with the Messenger of Allah on the day of Hudaybiyah, and had we seen fighting, we would have fought. That was during the truce between the Messenger of Allah and the polytheists. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Messenger of Allah and said: Messenger of Allah, are we not upon the truth and they upon falsehood? He said: Yes. 'Umar asked: Are not our slain in Paradise and theirs in the Fire? He said: Yes. 'Umar said: Then why should we accept a humiliating compromise in our religion and return before Allah has judged between us and them? He said: Ibn al-Khattab, I am Allah's Messenger, and Allah will never abandon me. 'Umar went away, unable to contain his anger, and came to Abu Bakr. He asked: Abu Bakr, are we not upon the truth and they upon falsehood? Abu Bakr said yes. He asked: Are not our slain in Paradise and theirs in the Fire? Abu Bakr said yes. He asked: Then why should we accept a humiliating compromise in our religion and return before Allah has judged between us and them? Abu Bakr said: Ibn al-Khattab, he is Allah's Messenger, and Allah will never abandon him. The Quran concerning the victory was then revealed to the Messenger of Allah. He sent for 'Umar and recited it to him. 'Umar asked: Is it a victory? He said: Yes. 'Umar was reassured and returned.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, who said: I heard Sahl ibn Hunayf say at Siffin: People, question your judgment. By Allah, I saw myself on the day of Abu Jandal. If I could have rejected the Messenger of Allah's decision, I would have done so. By Allah, whenever we took up our swords for a matter, it led us easily to another matter we recognized, except this matter of yours. Ibn Numayr's report does not include the words whenever we took up our swords.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq narrated this to us, both from Jarir. Another chain: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us. Both reported from al-A'mash with this chain. Their reports say: until a matter frightens us.

Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abu Hasin, from Abu Wa'il, who said: I heard Sahl ibn Hunayf say at Siffin: Question your judgment in matters of religion. I saw myself on the day of Abu Jandal. If I could have rejected the Messenger of Allah's decision, I would have. Every difficulty we entered into opened into another difficulty for us.

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, that Anas ibn Malik told them: When the verses were revealed: We have granted you a clear victory, so that Allah may forgive you (48:1), through His words: a tremendous triumph (48:5), as the Prophet returned from Hudaybiyah while they were weighed down by sadness and grief, and he had sacrificed the offering at Hudaybiyah, he said: A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the whole world.

'Asim ibn al-Nadr al-Taymi narrated to us: Mu'tamir narrated to us: I heard my father say: Qatadah narrated to us: I heard Anas ibn Malik. Another chain: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us. Another chain: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us. All reported from Qatadah, from Anas, with the like of Ibn Abi 'Arubah's hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Jumay', who said: Abu al-Tufayl narrated to us: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman narrated to us: Nothing prevented me from being at Badr except that my father Husayl and I had gone out. The disbelievers of Quraysh seized us and said: You intend to join Muhammad. We said: We only intend to go to Madinah. They took Allah's covenant and pledge from us that we would return to Madinah and not fight alongside him. We came to the Messenger of Allah and told him what had happened. He said: Return and fulfill their pledge; we will seek Allah's help against them.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim both reported from Jarir. Zuhayr said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, who said: We were with Hudhayfah when a man said: If I had reached the Messenger of Allah, I would have fought alongside him and done my utmost. Hudhayfah said: Would you really have done that? We were with the Messenger of Allah on the night of the Confederates, when a fierce wind and cold struck us. The Messenger of Allah said: Is there no man who will bring me news of the enemy, so that Allah will keep him with me on the Day of Resurrection? We were silent, and no one answered. He repeated the same call, and again no one answered. He repeated it a third time, and again no one answered. Then he said: Get up, Hudhayfah, and bring us news of the enemy. Since he called me by name, I had no choice but to rise. He said: Go and bring me news of the enemy, but do not provoke them against me. When I left him, I felt as if I were walking in a warm bath until I reached them. I saw Abu Sufyan warming his back by a fire. I placed an arrow on the center of my bow, intending to shoot him, but remembered the Messenger of Allah's words: Do not provoke them against me. Had I shot, I would have hit him. I returned, still feeling as if I were walking in a warm bath. When I reached him and told him the news of the people, and had finished, I became cold again. The Messenger of Allah wrapped me in the extra part of a cloak he had been praying in. I slept until morning. When morning came, he said: Get up, sleepyhead.

Haddab ibn Khalid al-Azdi narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd and Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik: On the day of Uhud, the Messenger of Allah was left with seven men from the Ansar and two men from Quraysh. When the enemy came close, he said: Who will drive them away from us and have Paradise—or be my companion in Paradise? A man from the Ansar advanced and fought until he was killed. The enemy came close again, and he repeated the call. Another Ansari advanced and fought until he was killed. This continued until all seven were killed. The Messenger of Allah said to his two companions: We have not treated our companions fairly.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, from his father, who heard Sahl ibn Sa'd being asked about the Messenger of Allah's wound on the day of Uhud. He said: The Messenger of Allah's face was wounded, one of his front teeth was broken, and the helmet on his head was smashed. Fatimah daughter of the Messenger of Allah washed the blood, while 'Ali ibn Abi Talib poured water over it with a shield. When Fatimah saw that water only increased the bleeding, she took a piece of matting, burned it until it became ash, then pressed it to the wound, and the bleeding stopped.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub, Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Qari, narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, who heard Sahl ibn Sa'd being asked about the Messenger of Allah's wound. He said: Indeed, I know who washed the Messenger of Allah's wound, who poured the water, and what was used to treat it. Then he related something like 'Abd al-'Aziz's hadith, except he added that the Prophet's face was wounded and said his helmet was broken instead of smashed.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar all reported from Ibn 'Uyaynah. Another chain: 'Amr ibn Sawwad al-'Amiri informed us: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi narrated to me: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad, Ibn Mutarrif, narrated to us. All reported from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, with this hadith from the Prophet. Ibn Abi Hilal's report says his face was struck; Ibn Mutarrif's says his face was wounded.

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: The Messenger of Allah's front tooth was broken on the day of Uhud and his head was wounded. He began wiping blood from it and said: How can a people prosper when they have wounded their Prophet and broken his front tooth, while he is calling them to Allah? Then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, revealed: You have no authority in the matter (3:128).

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, who said: It is as if I can see the Messenger of Allah recounting a prophet who was struck by his people. He wiped the blood from his face and said: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' and Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with this chain, except that he said: He was wiping the blood from his forehead.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah. Among those reports he said: Allah's anger became intense against a people who did this to the Messenger of Allah. He was pointing to his front tooth. The Messenger of Allah also said: Allah's anger became intense against a man whom the Messenger of Allah kills in the cause of Allah, Mighty and Exalted.

'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Aban al-Ju'fi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahim, Ibn Sulayman, narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: While the Messenger of Allah was praying near the House, Abu Jahl and some of his companions were sitting there. A camel had been slaughtered the previous day. Abu Jahl said: Which of you will get the stomach contents of so-and-so's camel and place them on Muhammad's shoulders when he prostrates? The most wretched among them went and got them. When the Prophet prostrated, he placed them between his shoulders. They burst out laughing and leaned on one another, while I stood watching. If I had had the strength, I would have thrown it off the Messenger of Allah's back while he was prostrating. He did not raise his head until someone went and informed Fatimah, who was then a young girl. She came and removed it from him, then turned on them, insulting them. When the Prophet finished his prayer, he raised his voice and supplicated against them. Whenever he supplicated, he repeated it three times, and whenever he asked, he asked three times. Then he said: O Allah, deal with Quraysh! three times. When they heard his voice, their laughter stopped and they feared his supplication. Then he said: O Allah, deal with Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt. He mentioned a seventh, but I did not retain it. By the One who sent Muhammad with the truth, I saw those he named lying dead on the day of Badr, then dragged into the well at Badr. Abu Ishaq said: Naming al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah here is a mistake in this hadith.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us. The wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. They said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Abu Ishaq narrate from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abdullah, who said: While the Messenger of Allah was prostrating and some people of Quraysh were around him, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt came with the stomach contents of a camel and threw them on the Messenger of Allah's back. He did not raise his head. Fatimah came, removed it from his back, and supplicated against whoever had done that. The Prophet said: O Allah, deal with the Quraysh leaders: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf—or Ubayy ibn Khalaf. Shu'bah was uncertain. He said: I saw them killed on the day of Badr and thrown into a well, except that Umayyah—or Ubayy—was dismembered and not thrown into the well.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ja'far ibn 'Awn informed us: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, with this chain and something similar. He added that the Prophet liked to repeat three times: O Allah, deal with Quraysh! O Allah, deal with Quraysh! O Allah, deal with Quraysh! He named al-Walid ibn 'Utbah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf without uncertainty. Abu Ishaq said: I forgot the seventh.

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah faced the House and supplicated against six men of Quraysh, including Abu Jahl, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, and 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt. By Allah, I saw them lying dead at Badr, changed by the sun on that hot day.
